title: Playing on trucks in Chicago with Punch Miller
summary: Howard tells how the excursion band advertised the dance on trucks at 47th and South Parkway, with Punch Miller jumping on to play.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Somebody told me once you played on a wagon up there at Adrigan. Yeah, that's the time, yeah. How was that? I never heard all that.
Man, man, that was the time. That's the time, Lee was waking up at their story up on Ramport Street, and they went for some other people. And anyway.
Well, Lee wasn't living up there then. No. He was from here. No, he was here. Because he had been up there and he's there now.

Yeah, but I, no, no, Lee was here. He was playing on that story. Yeah. And anyway, so we got out there, the two trucks, and we tied up on 47 and I think in, where the Riggle Theater at? South Parkway. Well, 47 and South Parkway. South Parkway, man, they never seen something like that in all their life. Boy, we tied up like we did back there in the olden days. And Bill, did we have a ball? And that's when Punch, Punch Miller, well he had been up there pretty good while. Punch Miller, we call him Kid Punch right here. Well, he came and he jumped on the truck because it looked like a person was kind of afraid of them people, you know what I mean?
And he jumped up there and, you know, got on the truck and- And played with me.
Yeah, yep. Because Lee was really so much sad.
Yeah, man, people like that, Ethel Warwick, all the people was around. Sure, all the the-ethical people. Yeah. Yeah, the-ethical people.
Yeah, man, man, boy, street was, they never seen that thing in all their life. And we stayed there for hours.
Is that the advertiser dance at the Warwick?

Yeah, that's right, the advertiser, I just remember where they were playing. They were playing other bands. Yeah, they were playing some other plays, that's right. And man, we had a sub-bomb. Oh, man. Yeah, we went all over Chicago on the trucks. And you just stay like we used to do, you know, and they just went from one corner to the mix. Stop up there, you play, I play, you play, I play, and that's the way the thing went. You see?
The big signs on your truck? Yeah. For sure. Of course. They sell any tickets in advance off of the truck or anything?
No, no, no, I wouldn't sell no tickets. There's no way it was that at all.
